newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Sundiro motorcycle 96 net triples.
newsitem.headline: China Sundiro motorcycle 96 net triples.

text.p: Hainan Sundiro Motorcycle Co Ltd, one of China's leading motorcycle makers, posted net profit of 219 million yuan ($26.4 million) in 1996, up 210.4 percent from 70.55 million yuan in 1995 on Chinese accounting rules.
Turnover was 1.68 billion yuan in 1996, up 95.1 percent compared with 862.8 million yuan in 1995, said the company's annual report published in Wednesday's Shenzhen-based Securities Times.
Earnings per share were 0.92 yuan based on 1996 profit, up 119 percent against 0.42 yuan in 1995, the company report said.

Sundiro planned a one-for-one bonus issue based on 1996 profit and capital surplus of 83.1 million yuan, it said, adding the company will table the dividend plan at a meeting of shareholders on April 6.
The company attributed the surge in profit to increased motorcycle output, which leaped 72.6 percent to 351,354 in 1996, as well as sales which soared 79.3 percent to 356,270.
Sundiro, one of 33 enterprises approved by Beijing to issue B shares, planned to make an initial public offering of 150 million B shares in the first half of 1997, the report said.

The company will appoint China Xinda Trust and Investment Co as chief underwriter, with Hoare Govett (H.K.) Ltd as the global coordinator, a company spokesman earlier told Hong Kong-based China Securities Bulletin newsletter.

Sundiro will use proceeds raised from the issue to upgrade production technology and facilities in its Hainan and Shanghai plants and set up joint-venture with Japanese firm Kawasaki to make motorbike engines, the spokesman said.
At the end of 1996, the firm had 237.4 million outstanding shares, consisting of 142.5 million legal person shares, 94.9 million A shares and 72,240 shares held by staff.
